Package com.codedstream.otterstream.experiments

Class ExperimentManager

java.lang.Object
com.codedstream.otterstream.experiments.ExperimentManager
public class ExperimentManager extends Object
A/B testing on top of OtterRuntime's existing canary mechanism (Milestone 6, LifecycleManager.deployCanary). This class does not route any traffic itself — that remains ManagedModel's job — it adds three things canary deployment alone doesn't have: a stable experiment identity independent of the underlying model version strings, outcome recording, and statistical comparison between control and variant.

One running experiment per modelId at a time — starting a second experiment for a model that already has one running fails fast rather than silently deploying a second canary on top of the first, which LifecycleManager.deployCanary itself would technically allow but which would make control/variant attribution ambiguous for this class's purposes.

Usage


 ExperimentManager experiments = new ExperimentManager(runtime);

 Experiment exp = experiments.startExperiment(
         "fraud-model-v3.3-rollout", variantConfig, 10); // 10% of traffic to the variant

 // In your pipeline, after each inference + rule decision:
 ExperimentGroup group = result.wasVariant() ? ExperimentGroup.VARIANT : ExperimentGroup.CONTROL;
 experiments.recordOutcome(exp.experimentId(), group, decision.confidence());

 // Later, check significance:
 StatisticalTest.ComparisonResult comparison = experiments.compareContinuous(exp.experimentId());
 if (comparison.significantAt95() && comparison.variantMean() > comparison.controlMean()) {
     experiments.concludePromote(exp.experimentId());
 } else {
     experiments.concludeRollback(exp.experimentId());
 }

Attributing which group served a given request: this class deliberately does not try to infer that for you — ManagedModel's canary routing decision (primary vs. canary) happens inside infer() and isn't exposed per-call today. Callers currently need their own way to know which group a given result came from (e.g. tagging the InferenceResult's metadata, or comparing the served model version against Experiment.controlVersion()/Experiment.variantVersion()). Exposing that routing decision directly from ManagedModel.infer() would remove the need for this workaround — tracked as a natural follow-up, not implemented here to avoid changing ManagedModel's public contract as a side effect of this module.

Since:
0.1.0

  • Method Details

    • startExperiment

      public Experiment startExperiment(String name, ModelConfig variantConfig, int variantTrafficPercent) throws DeploymentException
      Starts a new experiment: deploys variantConfig as a canary at variantTrafficPercent, and begins tracking it under name.
      Parameters:
      name - human-readable experiment name
      variantConfig - the candidate model configuration
      variantTrafficPercent - percentage of traffic to route to the variant (0-100)
      Returns:
      the started experiment
      Throws:
      ExperimentException - if an experiment is already running for this model
      DeploymentException - if the canary deployment itself fails validation/warmup

    • recordOutcome

      public void recordOutcome(String experimentId, ExperimentGroup group, double metricValue)
      Records one outcome observation for an experiment.
      Parameters:
      experimentId - the experiment this observation belongs to
      group - which arm served the request
      metricValue - the observed metric value — meaning is caller-defined, see class Javadoc
      Throws:
      ExperimentException - if the experiment id is unknown

    • compareContinuous

      public StatisticalTest.ComparisonResult compareContinuous(String experimentId)
      Compares control vs. variant as continuous metrics (Welch's t-test) — use for confidence scores, latency, or any real-valued measurement.
      Throws:
      ExperimentException - if the experiment id is unknown
      IllegalArgumentException - if either group has fewer than 2 recorded observations

    • compareBinary

      public StatisticalTest.ComparisonResult compareBinary(String experimentId, double positiveThreshold)
      Compares control vs. variant as a binary/proportion metric (two-proportion z-test) — treats every recorded metricValue >= positiveThreshold as a "positive" outcome (e.g. "flagged as fraud"), everything else as negative, then compares the two rates.
      Parameters:
      experimentId - the experiment to compare
      positiveThreshold - threshold at/above which a recorded value counts as positive
      Throws:
      ExperimentException - if the experiment id is unknown

    • concludePromote

      public Experiment concludePromote(String experimentId)
      Concludes the experiment by promoting the variant to primary (OtterRuntime.promoteCanary) — the variant won.

    • concludeRollback

      public Experiment concludeRollback(String experimentId)
      Concludes the experiment by discarding the variant (OtterRuntime.rollbackCanary) — the control stayed primary.
